issues.issue: Do the section 108 cessation provisions apply to country-of-asylum (resettled) protected persons, not only Convention refugees?
issues.applicant_position: Cessation under s. 108 cannot apply to country-of-asylum class members, who are not Convention refugees.
issues.respondent_position: Section 108 applies to all protected persons under s. 95, whatever the route by which protection was conferred.
issues.result_quote: the cessation provisions of section 108 apply to both Convention refugees and country of asylum or re-settlement class.

issues.issue: Does gaining permanent resident status on arrival protect him from losing it through reavailment?
issues.applicant_position: Permanent residence was granted on arrival, so any triggering conduct must have predated it; PR status cannot be lost through reavailment.
issues.respondent_position: Paragraph 46(1)(c.1) expressly provides for loss of PR status after a s. 108(2) cessation; the applicant's reading would make it meaningless.
issues.result_quote: This argument has no foundation in the legislative scheme.

issues.issue: Should the RPD have considered cessation under paragraph 108(1)(e)?
issues.applicant_position: The RPD erred by not considering 108(1)(e), a ground that does not cause loss of permanent residence.
issues.respondent_position: not stated (the court notes the appellant himself objected to any reference to 108(1)(e) before the RPD)
issues.result_quote: No error arises in the decision of the RPD not to entertain a ground of cessation which was neither advanced by the Minister or the appellant.
